title.narrative: Skills for Employment Investment Program Tranche 3

description.narrative: The proposed Tranche 3 (2020-2023) aims to harness and institutionalize training partnerships established under Tranches 1 and 2. It will continue to support sector-focused job-ready skills training through the existing partnerships with public institutes, industry associations and other organizations, covering skills requirements in 10 industry sectors. It will introduce selected advanced courses to adopt and adapt emerging Industry 4.0 skill requirements and help industries move up the value chain. It will also support new training specifically targeted at socially disadvantaged groups (including people with disabilities) and women entrepreneurs to ensure inclusive skilling efforts. Overall, Tranche 3 will train about 320,000 people, 30% of whom will be women. Tranche 3 will continue to support the operationalization of the National Skills Development Authority (NSDA) and the National Human Resource Development Fund (NHRDF) to sustain the SEIP efforts in building a strong skilled workforce.

title.narrative: Loan 3839: 100% of contracts awarded and 100% disbursed as of 10 May 2025

Progress Toward Outcome: Contracts and MOUs have been signed with the 12 industry associations, 5 public/NGO training providers and 4 EDC programs. The remaining BPs are at different stages of processing and will be completed soon.
Some results are in the Audited Project Financial Statements | Dec 2024: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/42466/42466-017-apfs-en_3.pdf
Some results are in the Initial Environmental Examination | Feb 2024: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/42466/42466-017-iee-en_0.pdf
Some results are in the Social Monitoring Reports | Mar 2025: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/42466/42466-017-smr-en_8.pdf

Status of Implementation Progress: Output 1:
Total number of new entrants enrolled up to 30 June 2022 was 79,527, and certified was 38,622. Out of the certified trainees, 23,514 were employed (60.88% of the certified).
The target of 3,000 trainees from socially disadvantaged groups has been split into two parts. PKSF has signed a contract to train 2,000 people. The other contract to train 1,000 disadvantaged trainees has again been divided into two parts, 400 people with disabilities and 600 orphans. Contracts for all the three groups have already been signed and the training has started for all of them.
Contract with BWCCI has been signed and training has started since 3 January 2021 with 2,650 female trainees enrolled, of whom 2,106 have so far been certified and 1,483 are placed in jobs (70.42% of the certified).
SEIP has already started the process of distributing special stipend to T3 graduates.
Output 2:
SDCMU has started to develop competency-based training standards (CSs), with a target of 55 CSs under Tranche 3, out of which 37 have already been finalized through validation. 21 CBLMs have been developed which are now ready for use.
194 Master Trainers (26 females) have already been selected, and training of 450 trainers will start after orientation of the Master Trainers. The first batch of ToT of 450 trainers is expected to start from August 2022.
SEIP is discussing next phases of training of trainers programs with international institutes (e.g., NYPI, ITEES), following on previous programs.
Output 3:
Finance Division approved organogram, recruitment rules, operational manual and TVET financing manual for NHRDF. NHRDF has already completed recruitment of some key officers. It is going to be fully operational by 2022.
Organogram of NSDA has been cleared by Finance Division. NSDA rules have been approved and posted in the website. Recruitment process has started.
Construction work has started for BITAC renovation and for BACI training center. Once the work is completed, the centers will be used for training delivery.
Output 4:
FinMan modules has been completed for improved financial management across training providers. Training and capacity development will be provided on the use of FinMan for relevant finance officers in training centers.
TMS system audit has been completed and further improvement is in process.
